lines: At every stage, an Adviser or Support can open L15: the versions a client is on, and why their last update said what it said.

A release's status: scheduled, live, replaced (a later release of its rule set is live; plans may still be on it), closed (no active plan is on it); or paused, then corrected. Every status change is logged: who, when, why.
1. Versions. A rule set's versions never change. A release makes one live from its effective date. The live version at any moment: the latest release live by then, neither paused nor superseded.

2. What holds a plan. A plan is the client's current plan snapshot, carrying the five rule set versions and the plan engine version; nothing else holds it. Risk profiling is stamped as of the last questionnaire, so a plan can read rs-1 after rs-2 is live (L15 shows both). The board stamps two today (G01: assumptions_version, instrument_set_version); the other three are added.
3. Reading. Plan screens read the current snapshot, H05 the waiting update; none calls the plan engine on opening. The one exception: net worth today, from holdings and prices as last updated.
4. Plan refresh. The inputs on file, the as-of time and the live versions go to the plan engine. The result is stored as a snapshot, compared with the current one, given an update type and shown.

5. What starts a plan refresh: a review done (Q01, Q05), a life event (Q06), a sharpen, the annual confirmation (Q04), a questionnaire retake, a staff edit or forced re-run (M03), a push, an app open past the max plan age, a release withdrawn or corrected.
6. At the next refresh: nothing runs at publish; the client_content job runs on the effective date.

7. Pushed now. The release picks plans with a running SIP into the fund, a pending action naming it, a verified holding of it, or a current snapshot made on a named release. The rollout job refreshes them in batches. It is idempotent per client and release, can pause and resume, and retries a failed client.
8. Scheduled: live by its effective date alone, since point 1 compares times. No midnight job has to succeed for new plans to be right.
9. The max plan age, checked at app open: a latest snapshot over 120 days behind a live Assumptions, Allocation or Funds release is refreshed on the inputs on file.

10. Pause, withdraw, correction. Point 1 skips a paused release. Withdraw refreshes, on the release before, every plan with an unaccepted update made on the paused release, and marks the old snapshot withdrawn. A correction is a new release; its rollout picks every plan whose current snapshot was made on the paused release.

11. Timing. A running refresh keeps the versions it read at its start. A client holding an update when it is withdrawn sees the notice on the next screen. A draft moves onto the new version when its rule set's live version moves.
12. Blocks. An overdue annual confirmation blocks a refresh (Q04 on the board); a lapsed account is frozen. LQ43: whether a pushed update gets past an overdue confirmation.
Calls made while building on 8 Oct 2026, open to veto: what moves and when, answering "19.2 becomes 18 or 22"; a release's life, asked for on the call.

lines: Finding a goal's cell: read its bucket on each axis from the client's inputs; the cell names the model portfolio. The completeness check proves on the draft that every cell is filled.

The completeness check walks every cell, the product of the bucket counts: 3 x 3 = 9 at launch, 3 x 4 = 12 after REL07, 3 x 4 x 2 = 24 in the discarded draft. Twenty cells (guessed on the 7 Oct 2026 call) means two axes cut finer, or three axes.
The allocation matrix has one row per cell, no "any" rows: 9 at launch, 12 after REL07 (with "any" rows, 7 and 10).
Model portfolios are fewer than cells, and sub-asset classes fewer than model portfolios, so a fund change is one edit however many cells exist.
A small cell has few goals; the impact preview marks it. A cut the client base cannot fill is a draft to discard (L03b).
A cell's history comes from the Allocation versions: its model portfolio in each release. No version is stored per cell.
Needs an app update: an axis on a field the app does not yet ask for. LQ5: a ceiling on axes and buckets.
The plan JSON contract (W03) carries each goal's risk_profile, horizon_bucket and model_portfolio_id in every plan snapshot.

lines: Store the result; never promise to work it out again: the plan engine version and the wording both change between the day of the advice and the day of the question.
A hash on every snapshot and release. The app's database role can insert into the record tables (the first table) but never update or delete.

Retention by class: regulated, as the nine records' Retention row says (LQ24); operational, to be decided: how long; derived, not kept (it can be worked out again). A deletion request (S25) leaves regulated records in place.

Look-ups the screens need: by client (L15: every snapshot in order, or the current one on a date); by release (L11, L08: every plan made on it, what each client was shown and did); by date (L08: each rule set's live version that day); by fund (L04: who was advised into it and still runs a SIP); by cell (L03: its history).
Which system holds the snapshot of record: LQ17 (proposed: the app).

Sizes per client a year: 8 snapshots x 60 KB plus 5 PDFs x 400 KB, about 2.5 MB. A year: 2.5 GB at 1,000 clients, 25 GB at 10,000, 250 GB at 100,000; five times that when kept five years or more (LQ28).
Calls made while building (logic plan, 8 Oct 2026), open to veto: hashes and an insert-only database role; three retention classes; sizes typed as examples, not evidence.

lines: Launch or later turns on one question: can it be added afterwards without losing anything? A version never stamped on a plan cannot be recovered; a chart over stored rows can be drawn any day.
Failure cases, and what the system does:
A refresh fails in a rollout: the job retries that client; L11 lists each failure by client.
A refresh during a pause: one starting after it uses the release before; one already running keeps the versions it read at its start.
gap, to be decided: whether withdraw or correction waits for refreshes still running
An update withdrawn while open: the notice shows on the next screen; a refresh on the release before replaces it, keeping the client's own changes; plan history reads "an update was withdrawn".

Three releases picked up at once: one refresh reads every live version at its start and writes one plan snapshot (Risk profiling: as of the last questionnaire). What changed is drawn against the current snapshot, a reason on every line; a house-view reason names its release. An update still waiting is superseded.
A refresh past the max plan age fails: the app opens on the old plan and tries again at the next open.
A blocked refresh (How a change reaches a plan, point 12): a lapsed account refreshes on return; the block is stored as an interaction (refresh_blocked) and listed on L08 and L15.
A revoked session ends at once: the next request is refused and logged.
A draft whose rule set moves (an urgent hold, say): it moves onto the new version, and its checks and impact preview rerun before approval.
A first plan made between publish and the effective date: it uses the live versions, then takes the release like any existing plan. LQ21: whether it should use the new values.
Calls made while building (logic plan, 8 Oct 2026), open to veto: the failure cases and what the system does; the launch and later split, answering "overkill".
